plans.objective: [DIM: structure] The solution space of a linear constraint system is uniquely rigid (dimension 0), so N_c(w) should remain flat as w increases, indicating that a small fixed network width suffices to satisfy all constraints without overfitting.

steps.description: Implement the rigid constraint family function for the numerical experiment. The hypothesis claims the solution space is uniquely rigid (dimension 0), so N_c(w) should remain flat as w increases. I need to define a family that corresponds to a rigid constraint system (low-dimensional/unique solution) to test this prediction. The family function must return training and validation points with correct (N,1) shapes and non-overlapping sets. I'll create a rigid system: a linear constraint system with a unique solution (e.g., a system of equations that has exactly one solution point). This will serve as the test case for the rigid hypothesis.

plans.objective: [DIM: structure] The solution space of a linear constraint system is uniquely rigid (dimension 0), so N_c(w) should remain flat as w increases because the network only needs to learn a single target function.

steps.description: [auto-routed: surprise=1.00] Implement the rigid constraint family (linear system with unique solution) and fat constraint family (linear system with infinite solutions) in the `family` function. Construct the rigid family as a system where w constraints uniquely determine the coefficients (e.g., w points on a line for a linear function), and the fat family as an underdetermined system (e.g., w constraints on a high-degree polynomial with many degrees of freedom). Ensure label shapes are (N,1), held-out sets are non-overlapping, and the zero-violation anchor is established at maximum width before N_c(w) scanning.
